1# DQStudio groups, subquivers and saved views
2
3The physical `DecayQuiver` remains the authority for levels and transitions.
4Studio keeps graph membership separate from view settings; every view references
5that same quiver. Branching populations, transition probabilities and detector
6calibration are document data and do not change when switching views.
7
8## Try it
9
10Import `examples/dqstudio-bands-demo.json`. It is a **synthetic illustration**,
11not evaluated nuclear data. Open **Saved views…** and restore the band overview,
12selected branch with context, or collapsed-band view.
13
14- **Quiver View** retains the ordinary level scheme.
15- **Band View** uses shorter levels in columns. Drag a band heading horizontally
16  to move all its levels. In **Groups…**, edit the band's centre and level width.
17  Right-click a heading or summary box to collapse/expand it.
18- **Focus View** displays a group, an explicit subquiver, or a level with selected
19  context. Choose the target in **Focus / energy / style…**.
20
21## Groups and explicit subquivers
22
23**Groups…** manages semantic collections of levels: bands, cascades and user
24categories. A group's default focus includes all transitions between its levels.
25Its colour and line style apply to member levels and intra-group transitions;
26individual styles override those defaults. For overlapping groups, the first
27membership determines layout and inherited style. Unassigned transitions retain
28the global style.
29
30**Subquivers…** manages explicit selections of vertices **and arrows**. Selecting
31an arrow also selects its endpoints. Other arrows between the same endpoints
32remain excluded. The “Select all arrows…” button explicitly builds an induced
33selection when wanted. Saving validates that every selected arrow has both
34endpoints selected.
35
36In **Focus / energy / style…**, context choices include incoming, outgoing,
37both directions, all ancestors, or all descendants. Incoming/outgoing/both use
38the chosen neighbour depth. Added context is faded; the original selection stays
39prominent. An explicitly excluded internal arrow stays excluded even when context
40is enabled. Focus is a visual restriction: analysis still uses the full quiver.
41
42Collapsed groups become summary boxes. External connections are retained and
43aggregated by their displayed endpoints; hover an aggregate line to see its
44original transition names. Labels count transitions, **not probabilities**.
45Internal transitions remain in the physical quiver and reappear on expansion.
46Hidden groups remove their displayed levels and incident arrows from the view.
47
48## Energy, style and camera
49
50Energy spacing is independent of wheel zoom:
51
52- **auto:** physical spacing when selected levels have known energies; otherwise
53  insertion order, retaining manual vertical placement for uncalibrated levels.
54- **physical:** spacing proportional to energy.
55- **compressed:** `log(1 + E/E₀)`, with editable positive `E₀` in keV.
56- **uniform:** even spacing in energy order when energies are known, otherwise
57  insertion order.
58
59An optional energy window filters levels and scales the selected interval.
60Explicit physical/compressed modes and energy windows require known energies;
61the settings dialog reports missing data instead of applying an invalid change.
62Enter energy in keV when adding a level, or use **Initial populations / energies…**
63to edit it later. Energies live in the core `DecayLevel` objects. Older
64`level_…keV` names and energy metadata are migrated once during import; renaming
65a level subsequently leaves its physical energy unchanged. An empty window displays a message.
66`Y ×` expands vertical spacing; wheel zoom changes the camera scale.
67Drag empty canvas to pan; **Fit** recovers the displayed scheme.
68
69Style precedence is **global → group → object override**. Global colour and
70transition label visibility are in the view settings dialog. Groups supply
71colour, stroke width and solid/dashed/dotted lines. Right-click a level or
72transition and choose **Style…** for independent overrides; “Inherit”/blank
73fields remove the corresponding overrides.
74
75## Saved views
76
77**Saved views…** saves the current configuration under a name. Saving an existing
78name replaces that view. Restore/delete operations apply to the selected entry.
79Views contain layout mode, focus/context, energy transform/window, group positions
80and widths, visibility/collapse, inherited and individual styles, camera centre
81and scale, object highlights, and manual level/transition offsets. Camera restore
82is subject to normal viewport/scrollbar pixel rounding. Calibrated energy spacing
83takes precedence over manual vertical positions.
84
85Group/subquiver definitions are shared across saved views. Editing membership
86therefore affects every view referencing that definition. Removing a definition
87clears references to it from all views. Removing levels remaps index references;
88removing transitions or changing their endpoints prunes invalid explicit arrow
89memberships and saved styles/offsets. Earlier Studio group metadata is migrated
90on import. Existing source JSON without view data remains supported.
91
92## Populations and efficiencies
93
94**Initial populations / energies…** edits initial level fractions, which must sum
95to one. They are stationary terms of the branching vector. The transition vector
96uses the quiver's editable transition coefficients, and their sum is the decay
97vector. Separate tables are available in the right panel. Populated levels must
98have their population redistributed before deletion.
99
100**Import Efficiency CSV…** accepts the GRIFFIN file in `data/GRIFFIN_Eff.csv`
101with its `Energy[keV], HPGe` header, as well as the generic format below. GRIFFIN
102values are used directly as efficiency fractions, not percentages.
103
104For each transition, Studio evaluates the curve at `|Esource − Etarget|` in keV.
105Exact tabulated energies use the corresponding sample; intermediate energies
106are linearly interpolated. **Show Transition Efficiencies** lists the transition
107name, derived energy and assigned efficiency. The map is rebuilt from the current
108level energies for every calculation, so editing an energy updates detection.
109The supplied GRIFFIN table covers 10–2000 keV; out-of-range transitions are reported
110by name and energy.
111
112Generic CSV format:
113
114```csv
115energy_keV,efficiency
1160,0.20
1171000,0.10
1183000,0.05
119```
120
121Supply at least two strictly increasing energies and fractions in `[0,1]`.
122Blank lines and `#` comments are allowed. Linear interpolation is used with no
123extrapolation. Missing energies or incomplete transition-energy coverage reject
124the import without replacing the prior curve.
125
126**Show Gamma Emission Probabilities** applies `1/(1+α)` to physical feeding
127using `metadata.conversion_coefficients`, keyed by transition name.
128**Show Detection Probabilities** then multiplies by the efficiency at the
129transition energy. Physical transition branches must include gamma + IC; they
130are not renormalized or efficiency-weighted during propagation. No summing
131correction is added by these controls. If no IC map is supplied, α=0 is assumed
132and the table title says so. A supplied map must contain every transition with
133a finite nonnegative coefficient. **Show Transition Efficiencies** also displays α.
134Saved views share these physical inputs.
135
136The `examples/133Ba_gamma_quiver.json` example includes all nine coefficients
137from `PhotonEvaporation5.5/z55.a133`, and explicitly sets initial populations to
1380.145 at 383.8491 keV and 0.855 at 437.0113 keV. Its integration-test generator
139preserves these inputs on every export.
140
141## Storage contract
142
143`metadata.groups` stores stable group IDs, names, semantic kinds, and level
144indices. `metadata.subquivers` stores stable IDs, names, level indices, and
145explicit transition names. `metadata.view` is the active view state;
146`metadata.saved_views` contains `{name, state}` entries.
147
148Each state stores `group_layout` keyed by stable group ID, `focus` keyed by
149selection type/ID (or a level index), `energy`, global/per-object styles, camera,
150highlights and manual offsets. Visual data never enters core `DecayLevel` or
151`DecayTransition` classes. Membership uses document indices/unique transition
152names; Studio remaps or prunes them on deletion. No public core subquiver API or
153algebraic restriction operator is introduced by these visualization changes.
154
155Physical populations and calibration remain in `metadata.branching` and
156`metadata.efficiency_samples`. Core level energies are exported in the top-level
157`level_energies_keV` array aligned with `levels`; `null` means unknown, while
158`0` is a known ground-state energy. Both native `DecayQuiver::ExportJson` and
159Studio use this format. Old files without the array continue to load; legacy
160energy metadata is migrated and removed. An explicit energy array takes
161precedence over legacy metadata and display names. JSON `analysis_vectors` contains named branching,
162transition and combined decay snapshots. Calculations rebuild from authoritative
163physical inputs rather than trusting snapshots. Custom path vectors rebind to
164current transitions after edits; invalid paths are discarded.
165
166
167## Core energy API
168
169```cpp
170DecayQuiver quiver;
171auto* ground = quiver.AddLevel("ground", 0.0);       // keV
172auto* excited = quiver.AddLevel("excited", 1332.5);
173auto* unknown = quiver.AddLevel("unmeasured");
174
175excited->SetEnergy(1332.492);
176const double gammaEnergy = excited->GetEnergy() - ground->GetEnergy();
177if (unknown->HasEnergy()) { /* safe to call GetEnergy() */ }
178unknown->ClearEnergy();
179```
180
181`DecayLevel(name, energy_keV)` is also available. Energies must be finite and
182nonnegative. `GetEnergy()` throws `std::logic_error` when unset; invalid setters
183throw `std::invalid_argument` without changing the previous energy. Unknown is
184never silently treated as zero. Names, path identity and probabilities retain
185their existing semantics. Nuclear-data builders assign the reader's full numeric
186energy, rather than recovering it from rounded level names.
187
188
189## Two-transition coincidence
190
191The right panel's **Two-transition coincidence** section selects two distinct
192transitions A and B. **Calculate Coincidence Probability** evaluates
193`DecayProbability::CoincidenceProbability` in both orders and adds the disjoint
194results for the acyclic decay graph. Reversing the selections gives the same
195joint probability. Mutually exclusive branches give zero; selecting the same
196transition twice disables calculation. All calculations use the full quiver,
197regardless of the displayed focus or hidden groups.
198
199The panel shows:
200
201- **Physical:** both selected transitions occur, counting gamma + IC.
202- **Gamma emission:** physical coincidence divided by `(1+αA)(1+αB)`.
203- **Detected:** gamma coincidence multiplied by `ε(EA) ε(EB)`, when a CSV is
204  loaded. This assumes independent detection efficiencies and does not include
205  angular correlations, detector-pair geometry or summing corrections.
206
207When IC data is absent, α=0 is explicitly indicated. Parallel arrows are resolved
208to their individual branching fractions because the core path form groups paths
209with the same endpoints. Selections survive ordinary edits where possible;
210results are cleared when inputs change, preventing stale values from being shown.
211
